title: Pitch Foundation
what: The five-stage shape of every pitch. Where you start before anything else is added on top.
remember: Mistakes do not break a pitch. Stopping does. Trust the structure to hold you.

title: S.E.E.N.
what: Smile, Eye Contact, Enthusiasm, Nodding. Your baseline — runs from approach to walk-away.
remember: S.E.E.N. is not something you switch on and off. It runs the entire time.

title: KISS vs KILL
what: Keep It Short & Simple vs Keep It Long & Lethal. Short sentences, then a question.
remember: If you have been talking for thirty seconds, you are already in KILL. Stop and ask a question.

title: The 5 Steps
what: Introduction, Problem, Solution, Close, Consolidation. The structure of every conversation.
remember: The five stages are not a script. They are the shape your conversation needs to take.

title: Objection Handling
what: A five-step deflection model. Most first objections are automatic, not genuine.
remember: An objection means the conversation is still alive. Treat it that way.

title: Impulse Factors (GIFTS)
what: Six triggers that build impulse: Greed, Indifference, Fear of Loss, Jones Theory, Sense of Urgency, Passion & Emotion.
remember: Your own passion is the most powerful trigger of all.

title: Impulse Curve
what: Maps the donor's willingness to act as it rises and falls through your pitch.
remember: If you cannot tell where the curve is, you are not asking enough questions.

title: Body Language & Tone of Voice
what: The basics of how you carry yourself — posture, hands, eye contact, pace, volume, pitch.
remember: If your body is closed, the donor's mind closes with it. If you sound flat, the donor feels flat.

title: Matching and Mirroring
what: Match the donor's energy in the first three seconds.
remember: A loud pitch at a quiet person is a closed door.

title: Intelligence & Rapport
what: One open question and — if it's genuine — one real compliment in every conversation.
remember: If the pitch fits everyone, it was built for no one. A real question always beats a forced compliment.

title: Emotional Control & State Management
what: Reset between hard doors. Keep showing up at full energy.
remember: The next door deserves a fresh version of you.
